summary: Lists requirements for a One-way Active Measurement Protocol. With good time sources, networks can measure one-way delay and loss precisely, and an interoperable protocol is needed. It is informational.

eli5.summary: Measuring how long a trip takes one way needs clocks that agree. This lists what a tool to test that must do.

questions: what are the owamp security modes
why separate owamp test and control protocols
subtitle: What a standard protocol for measuring one-way network delay and loss between vendors' devices has to do.

tldr.problem: Good time sources such as GPS now let hosts measure one-way delay and loss precisely, but there is no standard way for devices from different vendors to run such measurements together.
tldr.mechanism: RFC 3763 lists requirements for a One-way Active Measurement Protocol (OWAMP): split it into a test protocol and a control protocol, keep all raw data, support Poisson streams, and offer strong security options.
tldr.outcome: It is a requirements document, not a protocol. The protocol itself was left to a separate specification, and IANA matters are to go there too.

today: RFC 3763 is an Informational requirements document from April 2004, and it has not been obsoleted or updated. It specifies no protocol itself; it says IANA considerations belong in the protocol specification.

sections.title: Motivation and Goals
sections.content:
The IETF IP Performance Metrics (IPPM) working group has defined one-way delay (RFC 2679) and one-way loss (RFC 2680) metrics. Several measurement platforms collect them, but there is no standard for interoperability. This document aims at a protocol that lets users measure with devices from different vendors at both ends and still get meaningful results.

The enabling factor is affordable GPS and CDMA based time sources, which let hosts time-stamp packets with accuracy better than Internet delays. The authors envision open one-way measurement beacons that make one-way delay as commonplace as round-trip time measured with ICMP-based tools like ping. The RFC adds that even without very accurate timestamps, loss can be measured well enough for practical purposes such as network operations.
sections.eli5: If two toy walkie-talkies from different shops cannot talk to each other, they are not much use. A standard lets any two measuring tools work as a pair.

sections.title: Functional Requirements
sections.content:
The protocol should measure, record and distribute results for one-way singleton characteristics such as those in RFC 2679 and RFC 2680, within the framework of RFC 2330. Because those metrics are based on Poisson sampling, Poisson streams must be supported. Non-singleton characteristics and application traffic simulation need not be addressed.

The protocol should not require post-processing: all data from a session should stay available so that loss, mean delay, jitter, 90th percentile of delay and so on can be computed later from raw data. Results should be distributable separately from measurement requests, since the final consumer may be the receiver or a third host, and direct transfer to the destination should be possible.
sections.eli5: Keep every raw measurement, like writing down each lap time, so anyone can work out averages later in whatever way they like.

sections.title: Two Protocols: Test and Control
sections.content:
Setting up a session and running it are different tasks, with different needs and possibly different transports, so the RFC calls for two protocols: OWAMP-Test to conduct the measurement session and OWAMP-Control for session setup, teardown, confirmation and retrieval. Devices that support only OWAMP-Test should still be usable.

OWAMP-Test should be lightweight, allow UDP, support varying packet sizes and network services such as DSCP marking, carry only universally meaningful fields, carry data to calculate experimental errors in every packet and, if practical, produce packets small enough to fit in a single ATM cell when encapsulated.

OWAMP-Control should authenticate peers with a common method such as user ID and shared secret, schedule zero or more test sessions (not necessarily between the control peers), start sessions together or at scheduled times, retrieve results, and confirm completion or allow an abort. It should let peers tell network failures from peer failures.
sections.eli5: One part is the stopwatch race itself, kept very simple. The other part is the referee who sets up the race and collects the times afterwards.

sections.title: Limiting Packet Types and Scalability
sections.content:
Allowing arbitrary packet types would be an unmanageable security hole. Raw sockets cause higher loss on general purpose computers, a receiver filter would be hard to describe formally, a compromised identity could be used to send arbitrary traffic, and crafted packets could disrupt some link-layer protocols. So OWAMP is only required to support measurements with a given Differentiated Services Codepoint (DSCP, RFC 2474) or Per Hop Behavior Identification Code (RFC 3140).

On scalability, OWAMP should not make the problem worse or block scalable architectures. A full mesh of always-on measurements among N nodes needs O(N^2) resources, but deciding which measurements to run is the user's responsibility.
sections.eli5: The tool only needs to send ordinary test packets with a chosen priority label. If it could send any packet at all, a bad guy could misuse it.

sections.title: Security Requirements
sections.content:
Peers should authenticate with a user ID and shared secret, and outsiders must not be able to learn the secret or impersonate users by watching or tampering. Authorization normally rests on the authenticated identity, and different identities may have different testing privileges.

The design should make it hard for a middle party to flatter results by giving measurement packets special treatment, for instance a priority queue if OWAMP-Test traffic goes to a well-known port. The RFC compares this to restaurants spotting restaurant critics. OWAMP-Control must authenticate each message and resist replay. OWAMP-Test must measure duplication, so it cannot reject replays, since natural and malicious duplicates look alike.

Three modes are required: encrypted mode (all security mechanisms), authenticated mode (like encrypted but without encrypting timestamps, since that takes unpredictable time) and unauthenticated mode (no cryptography, with mandatory safeguards against capacity starvation and worm use, such as rate-limiting requests). Other options and modes should be kept to a practical minimum.
sections.eli5: Only people with the right password can start a test, and nobody should be able to tell which packets are tests, so they cannot give the test packets a faster lane.

cells: Like encrypted mode, minus timestamp encryption
